bib.title: Scheduled Sampling for Sequence Prediction with Recurrent Neural Networks

question: How can the mismatch between training (true previous token fed) and inference (model's own previous token fed) in recurrent sequence generators be reduced?
hypothesis: Gradually moving training from feeding true previous tokens to feeding the model's own samples makes the model robust to its own mistakes and improves inference quality.
contributions: Scheduled Sampling: a curriculum that flips a coin per token to feed the true or the model-generated previous token, with a decaying probability of truth
Experiments on image captioning, constituency parsing and speech recognition
Used in the winning entry of the 2015 MSCOCO captioning challenge

method.summary: During mini-batch SGD training of an RNN/LSTM sequence model, for each token a coin is flipped: with probability eps_i the true previous token is the input, otherwise a token sampled (or argmax) from the model. eps_i decays over training by a linear, exponential or inverse-sigmoid schedule. Gradient is not propagated through the sampling decision.
method.task: sequence prediction (image captioning, constituency parsing, framewise speech recognition)

datasets.name: MSCOCO captions
datasets.preprocessing: image embedded by a pretrained CNN (without last classification layer) similar to Ioffe and Szegedy; embedding treated as the first word; one of 5 captions picked at random per example

datasets.name: WSJ parsing data
datasets.split: F1 reported on WSJ 22 development set
datasets.preprocessing: parse tree linearised to a sequence of operations (Vinyals et al. 2014)

datasets.name: TIMIT
datasets.size: 3696 train, 400 validation, 192 test sequences; average length 304 frames
datasets.preprocessing: 40-dim log Mel filter banks plus first and second derivatives; 180-dim targets per frame from forced alignment with a GMM-HMM (Kaldi)

models.name: Captioning LSTM
models.architecture: one-layer LSTM, image embedding as first input

models.name: Parsing LSTM with attention
models.architecture: one-layer LSTM with attention (Bahdanau et al.)

models.name: Speech LSTM
models.architecture: two-layer LSTM plus softmax, framewise with acoustic input x_t

training.objective: maximise log likelihood of target sequence (Eq 4) with previous-token input chosen by scheduled sampling
training.epochs: speech: eps ramped linearly over ten epochs then held; baseline best validation at about 14 epochs, sampling models about 9 epochs
training.dropout: dropout variants compared for captioning and parsing; rate not stated
training.compute: not meaningfully slower or faster to train than baseline (footnote 3)
training.seeds: speech: 3 models per configuration, average reported; others not stated

other.schedule_speech: linear from eps_s to eps_e over ten epochs then constant
other.schedule_formulas: linear max(eps, k-ci); exponential k^i; inverse sigmoid k/(k+exp(i/k))
other.coin: flipped per token; per sequence was much worse

inference.decoding: beam search; beam size 10 for speech; captioning and parsing beam size not stated

metrics.name: BLEU-4, METEOR, CIDER
metrics.definition: overlap between generated and target captions; best over the 5 references

metrics.name: Frame Error Rate
metrics.definition: next step: ground truth fed to predict next frame class (validation); decoding: beam search best sequence (test)

eval.protocol: single development set per task; no significance tests reported

limits: Gradient is not back-propagated through the sampling decision; authors say this makes training not exact and may explain validation accuracy dropping after about 9 epochs in speech (future work)
Hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, schedule constants k and c, dropout rate, beam size for captioning and parsing) are not given
Single run per config for captioning and parsing, no significance tests
Speech results are framewise on HMM-state targets, not comparable to hybrid HMM systems
Authors cannot say whether the parsing gain comes from reducing mismatch or reducing overfitting
Later work showed the objective is inconsistent (not stated here; outside source)

terms.definition: randomly choose, per token during training, between the true previous token (probability eps_i) and the model's own estimate (1-eps_i), with eps_i decayed on a schedule
ablation where the model is only fed its own predictions during training
ablation sampling the replacement token from a uniform distribution instead of the model
